patch.description:
Takes ONE field, `name`. A token's scopes, capabilities, scope grants and constraints are fixed at the moment it is minted and cannot be changed afterwards — so a token you audited stays the token you audited, and a token whose reach is wrong is replaced rather than edited (`POST /pats` for a new one, `POST /pats/{id}/rotate` to change the secret while keeping the grants). Sending any other field is a 422 naming it.

201.description: A new token with the same name, scopes, capabilities, spaces, constraints and expiry — a NEW `id` and a new secret, readable once; the old id is retired. The old secret is refused from the next request (`graceMinutes` 0, the default), for both kinds; send `graceMinutes` (up to 10080) to keep it working that long so an integration can swap with no outage — `DELETE /pats/{oldId}` ends that window early. get.description:
Everything we hold about the CALLER as one downloadable JSON document: profile, memberships, sessions, posts, topics, pages, custom-field values and consent records. Served as an attachment, synchronously — it is a database read, not a job, so there is nothing to poll. Scoped to the caller’s own account and no other; the organization-wide equivalent is `GET /orgs/{orgId}/export`, and the orchestrator-driven one is `/privacy/executor/{orgId}/*`.

**Requires token scope: `read`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

post.description:
IRREVERSIBLE. Anonymises the caller’s account and revokes every session, including the one making the request — the session cookie is cleared in the response, so a client must treat a 200 as a logout. Confirmation is the account’s own email address in `confirm` (credentials live in Atlas, so there is no local password to re-check and a live session is what proves the human); anything else is a 400. Content the account authored is detached from it rather than deleted, so a forum thread does not lose its replies. Export first with `GET /users/me/export` — afterwards there is nothing left to export.

**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

userId.description: An existing member of the organization.

role.description: viewer, editor or manager. Required unless `customRoleId` is given.

customRoleId.description: A custom role whose capabilities replace the named role on this library.

effect.description: DENY shuts this person out of this library whatever their org role says.

post.description:

put.summary: Replace the library's content model

shape.description: The library-wide shape every content type inherits. Omitted: unchanged.

types.description: Every content type, by key. REPLACES the set; omitted: unchanged.

variant.description: With `blockType`: the variant whose rows hold the field (one its patch adds, or a block field it renames or drops). Only rows in that variant are migrated.

anyOf.description: The field at `from` is now called `to`; every stored value moves with it.

variant.description: With `blockType`: the variant whose rows hold the field (one its patch adds, or a block field it renames or drops). Only rows in that variant are migrated.

anyOf.description: The field is gone. Its values are hidden for 30 days (restorable), then dropped.

variant.description: With `blockType`: the variant whose rows hold the field (one its patch adds, or a block field it renames or drops). Only rows in that variant are migrated.

anyOf.description: Undo a removal still inside its 30-day window: the hidden values come back.
The content type `from` is now `to`; its entries move with it.
The block type `from` is now `to`; every row of it, in every entry, follows.

ops.description: What changed, where a diff cannot tell: a rename is not a removal plus an addition. Checked against both models.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 100. 500 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Where to continue from: pass back the `page.nextCursor` of the previous answer. Opaque — there is nothing inside one to construct or parse. Sending one also opts into the enveloped shape, exactly as stating `Forumulate-Version` does.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. from.description: The path to redirect FROM, relative to the space’s mount. A trailing `*` matches everything below it: `/old/*` matches `/old/a` and `/old/a/b`. The longest matching wildcard wins, and an exact rule always beats a wildcard.

to.description: Where to send it: a bare path (relative to this space’s mount) or an absolute `https://` URL, which means exactly what it says. A trailing `*` here carries the part the `from` wildcard matched — `/old/* → /new/*` sends `/old/a/b` to `/new/a/b`; without it, every match lands on the one address.

type.description: `redirect` (the default) sends the reader to `to`. `rewrite` serves `to` at the address that was asked for, without changing the URL. A rewrite names a path of this same space — an absolute `to` is refused, because a rewrite is not a proxy.

status.description: The redirect’s HTTP status: 301, 302, 307 or 308. Default 308 (permanent, keeps the method). Not allowed on a rewrite, which answers whatever `to` answers.

query.description: Query-string conditions. A map of key → exact value: every listed pair must be present for the rule to match (other keys are allowed). `"ignore"` — the default — matches whatever the query is. Among rules with the same `from`, the one with more conditions is tried first.

passQuery.description: `true` carries the incoming query string to the target (merged under any query the target already has); `false` drops it. Unset keeps it on a same-host redirect and drops it on an off-site one. A rewrite always keeps it.

redirects.description: The whole table, replacing what is stored — except the rules the platform wrote itself when a page or a collection was renamed, which are kept unless your list claims the same `from`. Renaming a collection moves one address — its hub, `/c/<slug>` — and we write that rule for you; the pages filed under it are addressed by their own slug within the space and do not move.

With `refs` (`entry:<id>,page:<id>`) it labels exactly those references instead, in that order, and ignores `q`; one the caller cannot see is left out.

onThisPage.description: Whether this document carries the "on this page" rail: `auto`, `always` or `never`. Beats the legal space theme’s `onThisPage`; `null` clears it. A page-backed document sets `onThisPage` on its page’s metadata instead.

customCss.description: CSS for THIS piece only, after the space theme so it wins. Sanitised and scoped to the reader exactly like the space `customCss` (`@import` dropped, no way out of the <style>).

theme.description: A partial theme for this piece — colours, palettes, fonts, typography, colorScheme, components, contentWidth, layout, motion, and (on a blog post) `post` — layered over the space’s (which is over the site’s). On a post, release, event or legal document `PATCH` it MERGES key by key like the space theme’s PATCH, and `null` clears at any depth (`{"paletteDark": null}`); a page’s metadata replaces it whole. Unknown keys are refused by name. `null` clears all of it.

shareImageUrl.description: The og:image / twitter:image for this piece, separate from its cover. Wins over the cover and over the generated social card.

jsonLd.description: Structured data for this piece, as JSON (object or array of objects). Replaces the automatic markup on this piece (Article/BlogPosting, Event, DiscussionForumPosting/QAPage, the roadmap item’s Article). `null` restores the automatic one.

customization.description: This document’s own `customCss`, partial `theme`, `shareImageUrl`, `ogTitle`, `ogDescription`, `twitterCard` and `jsonLd`. Keys merge; `null` clears.

post.description:
Takes the document `GET /orgs/{orgId}/export` produces and lands it here. Idempotent, matched by SLUG at every level — re-importing the same document SKIPS what already exists rather than making a second copy of it — and additive: nothing in this organization is deleted because the document does not mention it. Forum spaces carry categories (tree, slugs), pins, accepted answers, polls, reactions (one row per reactor), whispers and each post’s author and `createdAt`; a post body is block `content` or `markdown`. Authors resolve to a member of this org by id, then by `members[].email`; an address with no account becomes a staged placeholder, and an account outside this org is credited by name only. The reply counts what was created and skipped per level, how each author was attributed, and lists every row that was skipped or changed in `warnings`. Synchronous: for a large forum, queue it with `POST /orgs/{orgId}/imports` instead and poll the job. For declaring the shape of a site rather than restoring content, see `PUT /orgs/{orgId}/manifest`, which dry-runs by default.

**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

seed.description: Whether to create the starter structure this kind of space ships with. get.description:
The space’s own theme (not layered over its site’s). `warnings` lists what it says that the reader will not do well — `motion.targets` entries whose animation is neither a built-in nor a keyframe of this theme or its site (`code: motion.unknown_animation`), and colour pairs the theme sets that fall under WCAG AA contrast in a scheme it can be read in (`code: contrast.low`), and keys this space sets that its SITE owns — `chrome` and `whiteLabel` are drawn from the site while the space is in one (`code: site.ignored`, naming the site) — each with the `key`. Empty when there is nothing to report. `ignoredInSite` is present only while the space belongs to a site: the site-owned keys this theme sets, which are stored but not rendered until the space leaves the site (`[]` when it sets none).

**Requires token scope: `read`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

put.description:
Replaces this space’s theme wholesale — colours, type, element styles, the phone layer. Prefer the PATCH unless you are importing a complete theme, because a full write clears anything the stored theme had that your body omits.

A `motion.targets` entry naming an animation that is not a built-in, a keyframe in this theme, or a keyframe of the space’s site is refused: 422 `validation.failed` naming the key and listing every valid name. The answer carries `warnings` and `ignoredInSite` like the GET — a `chrome` or `whiteLabel` written to a space that is in a site is stored and reported as `site.ignored`, because the site draws those.

**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

enabled.description: `false` hides the switcher (the same as `placement: "none"`). Unset: shown.

placement.description: Where the content-language switcher sits: header (the nav bar's end) | header-start | header-overflow (the header menu) | sidebar | footer | content-top | floating | none. Unset: the surface’s own place (docs: sidebar; others: content-top).

style.description: `select` (unset): the reader dropdown, from the control tokens. `pills`: a row of links. `compact`: a tight row of codes (EN · ES).

names.description: How each language is named: native (unset, "Español"), english ("Spanish"), code ("ES").

flags.description: A flag before each name. Off by default.

flagCountries.description: The country whose flag stands for a language: `{ "en": "US", "pt-BR": "BR" }`.

locales.description: Which languages are listed, in order (codes; `default` = the original). Unset: all declared.

customLabels.description: A label per language code (`default` = the original), over `names`.

missing.description: When this page has no translation in a language: home (unset — that language’s front door), disabled (listed, not a link), hide (only languages this page is translated into).

remember.description: Keep the reader’s pick, so a page in another language offers its translation. Never changes a page’s own language. Off by default.

patch.description:
Deep-merges a partial theme onto the live one, so changing a single colour cannot clobber the rest. This is the write a settings panel should make.

**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.
patch.summary: Update the theme in a space

get.description:
Reports whether an unpublished theme is sitting on this space, who saved it and when, and whether the live theme has changed since (`stale`). A draft nobody can discover is a trap, so this is the call a console shows a banner from.

**Requires token scope: `read`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

400.description: The request could not be understood — a malformed header, path or query value (`request.malformed`). A value that was understood but is not acceptable is a 422 `validation.failed`.

401.description: No credential, or one that is expired or revoked (`auth.required`). Send a Bearer token or the session cookie.

403.description: Authenticated, and not allowed — always `rbac.forbidden`, whether what is missing is the capability, the token scope, or a resource the token is pinned away from. The message names the capability and, for a scope refusal, the scopes that would grant it. A refusal because of the PLAN is a 402 with `quota.exceeded`, not this.

404.description: No such thing — one of the ids in the path does not resolve, or resolves to something this caller may not see (`*.not_found`).

429.description: Rate limited — see the RateLimit-* headers.

put.description:
Stores this theme as a DRAFT. `settings.theme` — what readers see — is left byte-identical. Preview it with `?preview=<token>` on any reader address of this space.

**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

warnings.description: Values we ACCEPTED and then rewrote, one sentence each — a slugified tag, a normalised colour, a clamped range, a slug that was taken. **Absent when nothing was rewritten**, never `[]`. The same sentences are on the `X-Field-Warnings` response header. If this is present, something you sent is not what is stored; read the resource back rather than assuming your own value.

locales.description: Which languages are listed, in order (codes; `default` = the original). Unset: all declared.

missing.description: When this page has no translation in a language: home (unset — that language’s front door), disabled (listed, not a link), hide (only languages this page is translated into).

patch.description:
Deep-merges a change onto an unpublished draft — or onto the live theme if no draft exists yet — so a redesign can be built up and previewed before any reader sees it.

**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

delete.description:
Throws the unpublished draft away and leaves the live theme as it is. The undo for a redesign you decided against.

**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

post.description:
Moves the draft onto `settings.theme` and clears it, in one statement. Answers 409 `theme_draft.stale` when the live theme changed after the draft was saved — publishing would revert that change — unless `force` is true.

**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

theme.description: A structurally large type (a deeply nested or recursive union). Its full shape is served by the endpoint that produces it; `GET /docs/block-schema` covers the document block model.

data.description: The created resource again, under a key that is the same on every create — so a generic client needs one parser rather than one per endpoint. It is the SAME object as the key named after the resource (`page`, `article`, `topic`, …), which remains the canonical name.

post.summary: Make the theme draft live

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 100. 500 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Where to continue from: pass back the `page.nextCursor` of the previous answer. Opaque — there is nothing inside one to construct or parse. Sending one also opts into the enveloped shape, exactly as stating `Forumulate-Version` does.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

put.description:
Up to eight named alternate palettes a visitor may switch between, each a partial theme layered over yours in their browser and remembered there. Note the picker that offers them is mounted on forum reader surfaces only today, so storing alternates for a docs or blog space shows nobody anything yet.

**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.
put.summary: Replace reader themes in a space

warnings.description: Values we ACCEPTED and then rewrote, one sentence each — a slugified tag, a normalised colour, a clamped range, a slug that was taken. **Absent when nothing was rewritten**, never `[]`. The same sentences are on the `X-Field-Warnings` response header. If this is present, something you sent is not what is stored; read the resource back rather than assuming your own value.

The message names the capability and, for a scope refusal, the scopes that would grant it. A refusal because of the PLAN is a 402 with `quota.exceeded`, not this.

preset.description: The named layout the space's index wears. Valid values depend on the SPACE's type — see the table in this operation's description, or `GET /space-types/{type}/presets`. An unknown value is a 422 that lists the ones this type accepts.

piecePreset.description: The named layout ONE piece of the space wears. Only some types offer a choice; for the others any value is a 422 saying so. `GET /space-types/{type}/presets` lists them per type.

frontDoor.description: The front door's knobs, by key. Only the keys this SPACE's type declares, of the kind it declares — a toggle takes a boolean, a choice takes one of its values — plus `sectionOrder`. An unknown key is a 422 that names it and lists the ones this type has. `GET /space-types/{type}/presets` serves the whole set as data under `frontDoor`.

put.description:
**The layouts each type accepts.** `preset` and `piecePreset` are validated against the
space's own type, so the same word is legal for one space and a 422 for another. The same list is
served as data by `GET /space-types/{type}/presets` (and `GET /space-types/presets` for all of
them at once), which is the one to read if you are generating configuration. That route answers
FOUR vocabularies — `presets`, `piecePresets`, `shapePresets` and `frontDoor` (the keys the
type's front door accepts, and the values each one takes).

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 100. 500 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Where to continue from: pass back the `page.nextCursor` of the previous answer. Opaque — there is nothing inside one to construct or parse. Sending one also opts into the enveloped shape, exactly as stating `Forumulate-Version` does.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. from.description: The path to redirect FROM, relative to the space’s mount. A trailing `*` matches everything below it: `/old/*` matches `/old/a` and `/old/a/b`. The longest matching wildcard wins, and an exact rule always beats a wildcard.

to.description: Where to send it: a bare path (relative to this space’s mount) or an absolute `https://` URL, which means exactly what it says. A trailing `*` here carries the part the `from` wildcard matched — `/old/* → /new/*` sends `/old/a/b` to `/new/a/b`; without it, every match lands on the one address.

type.description: `redirect` (the default) sends the reader to `to`. `rewrite` serves `to` at the address that was asked for, without changing the URL. A rewrite names a path of this same space — an absolute `to` is refused, because a rewrite is not a proxy.

status.description: The redirect’s HTTP status: 301, 302, 307 or 308. Default 308 (permanent, keeps the method). Not allowed on a rewrite, which answers whatever `to` answers.

query.description: Query-string conditions. A map of key → exact value: every listed pair must be present for the rule to match (other keys are allowed). `"ignore"` — the default — matches whatever the query is. Among rules with the same `from`, the one with more conditions is tried first.

passQuery.description: `true` carries the incoming query string to the target (merged under any query the target already has); `false` drops it. Unset keeps it on a same-host redirect and drops it on an off-site one. A rewrite always keeps it.

redirects.description: The whole table, replacing what is stored — except the rules the platform wrote itself when a page or a collection was renamed, which are kept unless your list claims the same `from`. Renaming a collection moves one address — its hub, `/c/<slug>` — and we write that rule for you; the pages filed under it are addressed by their own slug within the space and do not move.

put.description:

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 100. 500 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Where to continue from: pass back the `page.nextCursor` of the previous answer. Opaque — there is nothing inside one to construct or parse. Sending one also opts into the enveloped shape, exactly as stating `Forumulate-Version` does.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

doc.description: The intro as a block document; `null` clears it. Or send `markdown`.

markdown.description: The body as Markdown (CommonMark + tables/task lists), converted server-side. Alternative to `content`. Blocks beyond plain Markdown (callouts, tabs, cards, steppers, columns, buttons, …) are written as `:::name{attrs}` directives — every directive, its attributes and how it closes: `GET /docs/markdown-dialect`. Up to 2,000,000 characters of Markdown — the same ceiling the importer, the create and the update doors all use, so an imported page can always be written back.

body.description: A synonym for `markdown` — the name a page write uses for the same thing.

translations.description: NUM-43: the intro in other languages, `{ "es": { "markdown": "…" } }` (or `doc`). Replaced whole; `null` clears. Without `doc`/`markdown` at the top level the original intro is kept.

customCss.description: CSS for THIS piece only, after the space theme so it wins. Sanitised and scoped to the reader exactly like the space `customCss` (`@import` dropped, no way out of the <style>).

theme.description: A partial theme for this piece — colours, palettes, fonts, typography, colorScheme, components, contentWidth, layout, motion, and (on a blog post) `post` — layered over the space’s (which is over the site’s). On a post, release, event or legal document `PATCH` it MERGES key by key like the space theme’s PATCH, and `null` clears at any depth (`{"paletteDark": null}`); a page’s metadata replaces it whole. Unknown keys are refused by name. `null` clears all of it.

shareImageUrl.description: The og:image / twitter:image for this piece, separate from its cover. Wins over the cover and over the generated social card.

jsonLd.description: Structured data for this piece, as JSON (object or array of objects). Replaces the automatic markup on this piece (Article/BlogPosting, Event, DiscussionForumPosting/QAPage, the roadmap item’s Article). `null` restores the automatic one.

markdown.description: The body as Markdown (CommonMark + tables/task lists), converted server-side. Alternative to `content`. Blocks beyond plain Markdown (callouts, tabs, cards, steppers, columns, buttons, …) are written as `:::name{attrs}` directives — every directive, its attributes and how it closes: `GET /docs/markdown-dialect`. Up to 2,000,000 characters of Markdown — the same ceiling the importer, the create and the update doors all use, so an imported page can always be written back.

body.description: A synonym for `markdown` — the name a page write uses for the same thing.

enabled.description: `false` hides the switcher (the same as `placement: "none"`). Unset: shown.

placement.description: Where the content-language switcher sits: header (the nav bar's end) | header-start | header-overflow (the header menu) | sidebar | footer | content-top | floating | none. Unset: the surface’s own place (docs: sidebar; others: content-top).

style.description: `select` (unset): the reader dropdown, from the control tokens. `pills`: a row of links. `compact`: a tight row of codes (EN · ES).

names.description: How each language is named: native (unset, "Español"), english ("Spanish"), code ("ES").

flags.description: A flag before each name. Off by default.

flagCountries.description: The country whose flag stands for a language: `{ "en": "US", "pt-BR": "BR" }`.

locales.description: Which languages are listed, in order (codes; `default` = the original). Unset: all declared.

customLabels.description: A label per language code (`default` = the original), over `names`.

missing.description: When this page has no translation in a language: home (unset — that language’s front door), disabled (listed, not a link), hide (only languages this page is translated into).

remember.description: Keep the reader’s pick, so a page in another language offers its translation. Never changes a page’s own language. Off by default.

post.description:
Queue an organization export to be imported by the worker, for a document too large to finish within one request; answers at once with the job to poll.

Takes the same document as `POST /orgs/{orgId}/import` and answers 202 at once with a job: `{ id, status: "queued", progress: { done, total } }`. The worker imports it with the same rules as the synchronous import (idempotent by slug, additive, authors and poll voters resolved to members or staged accounts). Poll `GET /orgs/{orgId}/imports/{id}` for `progress` (one unit per page and per topic) and, when `status` is `succeeded` or `failed`, the `summary` or `error`. Use this for anything that would not finish within 30 seconds — a forum of more than a few hundred topics.

**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

post.description:
Move a public roadmap here from Canny or Featurebase: send their export (CSV or JSON) and it is queued as a roadmap board, items in the matching lanes with their votes, comments, tags and ETA.

Body `{ source: "canny" | "featurebase", data, space?: { name, slug } }`. `data` is the export as the source wrote it: a CSV file’s text, or its JSON (Canny `{ posts, comments?, votes? }`; Featurebase `{ submissions | results, comments? }`, or a bare array of posts). Each post becomes a roadmap item: open / under review → SUBMITTED, planned → PLANNED, in progress → IN_PROGRESS, complete → SHIPPED, closed / rejected → DECLINED, anything else SUBMITTED (listed in `notes`). Named voters become votes by those people; the rest of the source’s count is kept as anonymous votes. A multi-board export makes one board per source board. post.description:
Returns a short-lived token and the URLs it works on — the space’s own custom domains first, then our platform path. Append it as `?preview=<token>` to any page of this space to see the draft as a reader would, on the address a reader uses. The token expires; mint another whenever you need one.

# Getting started

Install the SDK, then create your first page.

block-content.summary: Author with a block document — `content` as BlockDoc JSON

content.text: Install the SDK, then create your first page.

post.description:
Creates a page directly inside one collection, which is the usual authoring door: it saves you creating a page and then moving it, and the slug is derived from the title unless you name one.

**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

**A taken slug is reported, not hidden.** With `onSlugTaken: "suffix"` a page whose slug already exists is created at `slug-2`, and the response says so: `slugChanged: { asked, used }` plus a sentence in `warnings[]` and on the `X-Field-Warnings` header. `onSlugTaken: "fail"` gives a `409 page.slug_taken` instead. **Unset, it is versioned:** `suffix` for a caller stating a `Forumulate-Version` before `2026-12-01` (or none), `fail` from `2026-12-01` — the safe default, and the blog's. `PATCH …/pages/{pageId}` takes the same option with the SAME default, so one rule covers both doors. See [Slugs](https://forumulate.com/guides/api-conventions#slugs).

**Send ONE body field.** `content` (block JSON) is exclusive with `body` and `sections` (Markdown); sending `content` alongside either is a 422 naming both. It used to accept them together and silently discard the block document. `body` and `sections` together remain legal — that is the designed authoring path (slots first, then trailing prose).

**A `parentId` must exist here.** A page id that is not a live page in this space is a 404, and one in another collection is a 422. A nil uuid used to be stored, producing a row that never appeared in the tree.

**A `sections` key must be a slot this space type declares.** An unknown key is a 422 listing the slots that exist; it used to create one that nothing renders.

**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

It is opaque and changes on any change to the resource (body, title, slug, `locale`, metadata). onSlugTaken.description: What to do when the slug you asked for is taken. `suffix` renames to the next free name — `install-2` — and returns it as `slug` with a `slugChanged` and a `warnings[]` entry. `fail` answers `409 page.slug_taken` and writes nothing, which is what a pipeline that must stay idempotent wants. Unset, the default depends on the `Forumulate-Version` you state: `suffix` before `2026-12-01` (and with no header), `fail` from `2026-12-01` — the same 409 a blog post gives.

patch.description:
**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

**A taken slug is reported, not hidden — the same rule as on create.** The default is versioned like create's — `suffix` before `2026-12-01` (or with no `Forumulate-Version`), `fail` from `2026-12-01`. With `suffix` a rename onto a slug that already exists lands at `slug-2`, and the ANSWER says where — `slug` is the slug the page now has, `slugChanged: { asked, used }` names both, and `warnings[]` and the `X-Field-Warnings` header carry a sentence. Read `slug`; do not assume the slug you sent. Send `onSlugTaken: "fail"` for a `409 page.slug_taken` instead. This door used to default to `fail` while create defaulted to `suffix`, and used to answer a bare `{ "ok": true }` with the new slug only on the header — so a caller who got `install-2` had to re-read the page to find its address. See [Slugs](https://forumulate.com/guides/api-conventions#slugs).

get.description:
Read a page: its id, metadata, `status` (`published`/`draft`), and a stable `contentHash` of the published body — so a docs-as-code pipeline can detect drift (a UI edit since it last pushed) without downloading the document. Add `?include=content` to also get the live block document as `content`.

**Requires token scope: `read`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

`status` is derived from the LIVE revision (`published` once anything has been published), so it does not change when a newer draft is saved — read `hasDraft` and `draftUpdatedAt` for that. Both were missing, and a pipeline reading `published` on a page whose latest work was unpublished had no way to tell.

anyOf.description: The parameters this page’s space type declares. parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Deleted pages per page, once a version is stated. Defaults to 500. 1000 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

anyOf.description: This is the pre-envelope shape, served only to callers who state no `forumulate-version`. It stops being served on 2027-09-01 — the same date this operation's `Sunset` response header carries. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to get the `page` envelope instead, which is the variant beside this one.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

anyOf.description: The enveloped shape, served to callers who state `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` or who send a `cursor`. It is the shape this route keeps after 2027-09-01, when stating no version starts answering it too.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

editorial.description: Your claim that this publish changes no substance — a typo, a broken link, formatting. For a page bound to a legal role it records an attributed amendment to the edition in force instead of issuing a new one, so readers who already accepted are not asked again. Publish the current draft of this page. **No request body.** 

**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

**References are resolved here.** A page whose body refers to a reusable snippet or an extension block that does not resolve is a 422 naming it. Saving a draft only warns (`X-Field-Warnings`), because dropping a snippet block in before creating the snippet is an ordinary order of work — but a reader must never be shown a block that renders as nothing.

relayout.description: Re-lay-out the reference already imported from this spec into the tree `landing`, `tagPages` and `slugStyle` now describe (`mode: "per-operation"` only). Existing operation pages are MOVED and RENAMED in place — their ids and bodies are kept, and every changed address gets an automatic 308 redirect; only tag and landing pages are created or deleted. The pages are found through `specId` when given, else as the generated pages in the target collection. The answer adds `moved` and `renamed`. With `dryRun`, nothing is written and the counts say what would happen.

**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

The uploaded `file` may be **JSON or YAML** — the same reader the inline `spec` field and the `sourceUrl` fetch use. It used to be `JSON.parse` alone, answering 400 "convert a YAML spec to JSON first", which is how most people keep a spec. A file that parses but is not an OpenAPI document (no `openapi`/`swagger`, nothing to generate from) is a 422 here too, rather than an empty reference written with a 200.

`mode` is `single | per-operation | per-tag` and `onExisting` is `fail | skip | replace` (default `fail` — this importer writes generated pages in one transaction, so refusing costs nothing and is all-or-nothing). Both used to be cast through unchecked, so a bogus `mode` silently took the single-page branch. `dryRun` and `replaceCollection` take the boolean spellings above; anything else is a 422.

parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 100. 500 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Where to continue from: pass back the `page.nextCursor` of the previous answer. Opaque — there is nothing inside one to construct or parse. Sending one also opts into the enveloped shape, exactly as stating `Forumulate-Version` does.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

200.description: Import counters. `files` is how many files the request carried — the denominator. `created` (new pages), `replaced` (existing pages rewritten in place), `skipped` (left untouched) and `failed` (could not be turned into a page) are DISJOINT and satisfy `created + replaced + skipped + failed === files`. `imported` is NOT "files processed": it is a convenience total meaning `created + replaced` — the pages this run actually wrote — so it EXCLUDES skipped and failed, and it OVERLAPS `replaced`. That overlap is why three files all rewritten answer `files: 3, created: 0, replaced: 3, imported: 3`: three pages, not six. Sum the disjoint four; never add `imported` to `replaced`. (An earlier version of this page documented `imported + replaced + skipped + failed === files.length`; that invariant is withdrawn — it stopped being true once a replace began counting as an import.) `collisions`/`prunedSlugs`/`plan`/`dryRun` appear when the request asks for them. `redirects` and `retired` appear when a file DECLARED an address change: see the request body for `slug:` and `redirect_from:`. `redirects` lists the rules the run wrote into the space's redirect table; `retired` lists the slugs it moved to the trash because a rule took over their address (reversible with `POST …/{pageId}/restore`). On a dry run both say what WOULD happen and nothing is written.

content.description: Up to 2,000,000 characters of Markdown — the same ceiling the importer, the create and the update doors all use, so an imported page can always be written back.

replaceCollection.description: Empty the target collection BEFORE importing (hard reset). Prefer `prune` for sync.

onExisting.description: What to do about a slug the SPACE already has (resolved space-wide, never per-collection): `replace` (the default) updates the existing page in place; `fail` writes nothing over it and lists its slug under `refused` (the default of `POST …/openapi/import`, offered here so one explicit value makes both importers behave identically); `skip` leaves it untouched; `rename` is the ONLY value that auto-suffixes to a free slug like `getting-started-2` (opt-in — a page at a URL nobody wrote is the worst docs-as-code outcome); `duplicate` is the legacy spelling of `rename`. An unrecognised value is a 422, never a silent `replace`.

prune.description: Sync mode. After importing, soft-delete (to trash) every live page in this scope the run did not create/replace/skip — so deleting a source file makes its published page disappear. `collection` scopes to the target collection; `space` to the whole space.

dryRun.description: Plan only. Returns what WOULD happen — the same counts (`imported` counts creates AND replaces, so `imported`+`skipped`+`failed` == files.length and `replaced` is a subset of `imported`), a per-file `plan`, cross-collection `collisions`, and the `prunedSlugs` a prune would remove — and writes nothing. `dryRun: true` sets `dryRun` on the response.

schema.description:
**A Markdown file may declare its own address.** Two frontmatter keys are read, and unknown keys are still ignored:

- `slug:` — the address this file lands at, instead of the one its filename spells. Slugified, so `Billing & Plans` and `billing-and-plans` are the same address; a value with nothing a URL can hold in it is refused with the file named, never quietly renamed. Two files declaring one slug is a `422`.
- `redirect_from:` — the addresses this page REPLACES, comma-separated, each rooted and relative to the space's mount (`/old-page`, never `/docs/old-page` — the reader prepends the mount itself). The import writes a redirect rule for each one and moves the page that answered there to the trash, because a rule alone leaves the old page in the sitemap, `llms.txt` and search. Both are reported on the response as `redirects` and `retired`. A self-redirect, a duplicate or a loop is a `422`, exactly as it is on `PUT …/redirects`; an operator's own manual rule for that address is left alone.

post.description:
Writes a batch of pages from Markdown or block JSON in one transaction, creating the collections they need. The door a migration or a git sync drives; it reports what it would do first if you ask for a dry run.

**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

`onExisting` is `fail | replace | skip | rename | duplicate` and defaults to `replace` (this importer syncs authored files per file, and the first import of a repo routinely lands on the starter page a new space ships with). **An unrecognised value is now a 422** — it used to fall through to `replace`, so a typo chose the destructive option. `fail` refuses to write over an existing page, counts it in `failed`, lists its slug in `refused[]`, and keeps `prune` from deleting it.

On the multipart doors, `dryRun` and the rest are read exactly as strictly as the JSON fields of the same name: `true/false/1/0/yes/no/on/off`, and anything else is a 422. `dryRun=maybe` used to run a REAL import.

newPages.description: What to do with pages created since the snapshot. `keep` (the default) leaves them published and reports how many there are as `addedSince`. `unpublish` takes them out of the reader so the space matches the snapshot; the pages and their revisions stay, so publishing one again is a single call.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Notifications per page, once a version is stated. Defaults to 100. 500 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.name: unread
parameters.description: Use true or false (true/1/yes/on and false/0/no/off are accepted).

anyOf.description: This is the pre-envelope shape, served only to callers who state no `forumulate-version`. It stops being served on 2027-09-01 — the same date this operation's `Sunset` response header carries. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to get the `page` envelope instead, which is the variant beside this one.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

anyOf.description: The enveloped shape, served to callers who state `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` or who send a `cursor`. It is the shape this route keeps after 2027-09-01, when stating no version starts answering it too.

data.overview: Install the SDK, then call it.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

**Requires token scope: `read`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

warnings.description: Values we ACCEPTED and then rewrote, one sentence each — a slugified tag, a normalised colour, a clamped range, a slug that was taken. **Absent when nothing was rewritten**, never `[]`. oneOf.description: The block-JSON form of this body. Send `content` and no `markdown`; sending both is a 422.

markdown.description: The body as Markdown (CommonMark + tables/task lists), converted server-side. Alternative to `content`. Blocks beyond plain Markdown (callouts, tabs, cards, steppers, columns, buttons, …) are written as `:::name{attrs}` directives — every directive, its attributes and how it closes: `GET /docs/markdown-dialect`. Up to 2,000,000 characters of Markdown — the same ceiling the importer, the create and the update doors all use, so an imported page can always be written back.

oneOf.description: The Markdown form of the same body, converted server-side into the same blocks. Send `markdown` and no `content`; sending both is a 422.

schema.description: `content` and `markdown` are ALTERNATIVES: send one of them. `markdown` is converted into the same block document `content` carries, so the resource that comes back is identical either way. Sending both is a 422 — nothing silently wins, because a client that sent the wrong field would otherwise see a 201 and the wrong body.

409.description: Refused because of the state this already is in — a name or slug already taken, a resource that already exists, or a precondition on the thing itself (`conflict`, `*.taken`, `*.exists`). Unlike a 422 the body is fine; unlike a 503 retrying it unchanged will not help.

bylines.description: Every name this post credits, in order (at most 10, counting co-author accounts). Each is `{name, role?, url?, avatarUrl?, bio?}` or `{author: <registry key>}` (the space’s author registry fills the rest). `byline` is the alias of the first; `null` clears the list.

sections.description: Markdown per section of the piece, keyed by the section key its shape declares. A BLOG article ships two, BOTH REQUIRED: `standfirst` (the line listings and link previews show) and `body` (the post). A space can add or rename its own — the keys for one are at `GET /space-types/{type}/slots` (and the space’s own shape). Combined with `markdown`, which follows the sections as ordinary prose.

onThisPage.description: Whether THIS piece carries the "on this page" rail: `auto` (the surface default), `always` or `never`. Beats the space theme’s `onThisPage`; `null` clears it back to the space’s.

customCss.description: CSS for THIS piece only, after the space theme so it wins. Sanitised and scoped to the reader exactly like the space `customCss` (`@import` dropped, no way out of the <style>).

theme.description: A partial theme for this piece — colours, palettes, fonts, typography, colorScheme, components, contentWidth, layout, motion, and (on a blog post) `post` — layered over the space’s (which is over the site’s). On a post, release, event or legal document `PATCH` it MERGES key by key like the space theme’s PATCH, and `null` clears at any depth (`{"paletteDark": null}`); a page’s metadata replaces it whole. Unknown keys are refused by name. `null` clears all of it.

shareImageUrl.description: The og:image / twitter:image for this piece, separate from its cover. Wins over the cover and over the generated social card.

jsonLd.description: Structured data for this piece, as JSON (object or array of objects). Replaces the automatic markup on this piece (Article/BlogPosting, Event, DiscussionForumPosting/QAPage, the roadmap item’s Article). `null` restores the automatic one.

customization.description: This piece’s own look and share card: `customCss`, `theme` (partial), `shareImageUrl`, `ogTitle`, `ogDescription`, `twitterCard`, `jsonLd`. Keys merge on write; `null` clears one key, or every key when sent for the whole object.

oneOf.description: The block-JSON form of this body. Send `content` and no `markdown`; sending both is a 422.

bylines.description: Every name this post credits, in order (at most 10, counting co-author accounts). Each is `{name, role?, url?, avatarUrl?, bio?}` or `{author: <registry key>}` (the space’s author registry fills the rest). `byline` is the alias of the first; `null` clears the list.

Blocks beyond plain Markdown (callouts, tabs, cards, steppers, columns, buttons, …) are written as `:::name{attrs}` directives — every directive, its attributes and how it closes: `GET /docs/markdown-dialect`. Up to 2,000,000 characters of Markdown — the same ceiling the importer, the create and the update doors all use, so an imported page can always be written back.

A BLOG article ships two, BOTH REQUIRED: `standfirst` (the line listings and link previews show) and `body` (the post). On a post, release, event or legal document `PATCH` it MERGES key by key like the space theme’s PATCH, and `null` clears at any depth (`{"paletteDark": null}`); a page’s metadata replaces it whole. Unknown keys are refused by name. `null` clears all of it.

shareImageUrl.description: The og:image / twitter:image for this piece, separate from its cover. Wins over the cover and over the generated social card.

jsonLd.description: Structured data for this piece, as JSON (object or array of objects). Replaces the automatic markup on this piece (Article/BlogPosting, Event, DiscussionForumPosting/QAPage, the roadmap item’s Article). `null` restores the automatic one.

customization.description: This piece’s own look and share card: `customCss`, `theme` (partial), `shareImageUrl`, `ogTitle`, `ogDescription`, `twitterCard`, `jsonLd`. Keys merge on write; `null` clears one key, or every key when sent for the whole object.

oneOf.description: The Markdown form of the same body, converted server-side into the same blocks. Send `markdown` and no `content`; sending both is a 422.

schema.description: `content` and `markdown` are ALTERNATIVES: send one of them. `markdown` is converted into the same block document `content` carries, so the resource that comes back is identical either way. Sending both is a 422 — nothing silently wins, because a client that sent the wrong field would otherwise see a 201 and the wrong body.

bylines.description: Every name this post credits, in order (at most 10, counting co-author accounts). Each is `{name, role?, url?, avatarUrl?, bio?}` or `{author: <registry key>}` (the space’s author registry fills the rest). `byline` is the alias of the first; `null` clears the list.

sections.description: Markdown per section of the piece, keyed by the section key its shape declares. A BLOG article ships two, BOTH REQUIRED: `standfirst` (the line listings and link previews show) and `body` (the post). A space can add or rename its own — the keys for one are at `GET /space-types/{type}/slots` (and the space’s own shape). Combined with `markdown`, which follows the sections as ordinary prose.

onThisPage.description: Whether THIS piece carries the "on this page" rail: `auto` (the surface default), `always` or `never`. Beats the space theme’s `onThisPage`; `null` clears it back to the space’s.

customCss.description: CSS for THIS piece only, after the space theme so it wins. Sanitised and scoped to the reader exactly like the space `customCss` (`@import` dropped, no way out of the <style>).

theme.description: A partial theme for this piece — colours, palettes, fonts, typography, colorScheme, components, contentWidth, layout, motion, and (on a blog post) `post` — layered over the space’s (which is over the site’s). On a post, release, event or legal document `PATCH` it MERGES key by key like the space theme’s PATCH, and `null` clears at any depth (`{"paletteDark": null}`); a page’s metadata replaces it whole. Unknown keys are refused by name. `null` clears all of it.

shareImageUrl.description: The og:image / twitter:image for this piece, separate from its cover. Wins over the cover and over the generated social card.

jsonLd.description: Structured data for this piece, as JSON (object or array of objects). Replaces the automatic markup on this piece (Article/BlogPosting, Event, DiscussionForumPosting/QAPage, the roadmap item’s Article). `null` restores the automatic one.

oneOf.description: The block-JSON form of this body. Send `content` and no `markdown`; sending both is a 422.

oneOf.description: The block-JSON form of this body. Send `content` and no `markdown`; sending both is a 422.

markdown.description: The body as Markdown (CommonMark + tables/task lists), converted server-side. Alternative to `content`. Blocks beyond plain Markdown (callouts, tabs, cards, steppers, columns, buttons, …) are written as `:::name{attrs}` directives — every directive, its attributes and how it closes: `GET /docs/markdown-dialect`. Up to 2,000,000 characters of Markdown — the same ceiling the importer, the create and the update doors all use, so an imported page can always be written back.

oneOf.description: The Markdown form of the same body, converted server-side into the same blocks. Send `markdown` and no `content`; sending both is a 422.

schema.description: `content` and `markdown` are ALTERNATIVES: send one of them. `markdown` is converted into the same block document `content` carries, so the resource that comes back is identical either way. Sending both is a 422 — nothing silently wins, because a client that sent the wrong field would otherwise see a 201 and the wrong body.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Articles per page. Defaults to 20. 100 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Which page of results to return, 1-based. Out-of-range pages return an empty list.

parameters.name: pinned
parameters.description: Use true or false (true/1/yes/on and false/0/no/off are accepted).

parameters.name: featured
parameters.description: Use true or false (true/1/yes/on and false/0/no/off are accepted).

parameters.name: exclude
parameters.description: Comma-separated post ids to leave out — a front page’s feeds de-duplicating each other.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Skip this many posts before the page starts (added to the page’s own offset).

anyOf.description: This is the pre-envelope shape, served only to callers who state no `forumulate-version`. It stops being served on 2027-09-01 — the same date this operation's `Sunset` response header carries. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to get the `page` envelope instead, which is the variant beside this one.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

topics.description: The same rows as `articles`, under the name the forum uses for the same objects — a blog article IS a topic underneath (same fields), so a client written against the forum reads the blog unchanged. Present whenever `page` is.

anyOf.description: The enveloped shape, served to callers who state `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` or who send a `cursor`. It is the shape this route keeps after 2027-09-01, when stating no version starts answering it too.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

minValue.description: Lowest number a voter may pick. With maxValue/step the range must span 2–20 steps.

maxValue.description: Highest number a voter may pick. Must be greater than minValue.

step.description: Spacing between pickable numbers (default 1). Widen it to keep the range inside 20 steps.

closesAt.description: When voting closes. Must be in the future — a past date created an already-closed poll.

customCss.description: CSS for THIS piece only, after the space theme so it wins. Sanitised and scoped to the reader exactly like the space `customCss` (`@import` dropped, no way out of the <style>).

theme.description: A partial theme for this piece — colours, palettes, fonts, typography, colorScheme, components, contentWidth, layout, motion, and (on a blog post) `post` — layered over the space’s (which is over the site’s). On a post, release, event or legal document `PATCH` it MERGES key by key like the space theme’s PATCH, and `null` clears at any depth (`{"paletteDark": null}`); a page’s metadata replaces it whole. customization.description: This piece’s own look and share card: `customCss`, `theme` (partial), `shareImageUrl`, `ogTitle`, `ogDescription`, `twitterCard`, `jsonLd`. Keys merge on write; `null` clears one key, or every key when sent for the whole object.

post.description:
Creates a category in this forum: `name`, `description`, `color`, `parentId`, `logoUrl`, `backgroundUrl`. The plan limit on categories counts per community space, so a 402 names this space’s count and the most one community may hold.

**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.
post.summary: Create a category in a space

warnings.description: Values we ACCEPTED and then rewrote, one sentence each — a slugified tag, a normalised colour, a clamped range, a slug that was taken. **Absent when nothing was rewritten**, never `[]`. The same sentences are on the `X-Field-Warnings` response header. If this is present, something you sent is not what is stored; read the resource back rather than assuming your own value.

patch.description:
Changes a category: any field `POST …/forum/categories` takes, plus its look and `topicKind` — `"question"` makes its topics count toward the automatic Q&A look and files new topics there as questions; `null` clears a field.

**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: Delete a category that still holds topics and leave those topics uncategorised. Without this (or `moveTo`) such a delete is refused with 409.

parameters.name: moveTo
parameters.description: Re-file this category's topics under this category (which must be in the same space) before deleting it.

parameters.name: spaceId
parameters.description: The space: its uuid, or its slug within the organization. It is not decoration on a nested route — an id further down the path that belongs to a DIFFERENT space is a 404, not a cross-space read, which is why the operations that never bound this parameter still had to declare it.

200.description: Deleted. `topics` is how many topics the delete affected — moved to `movedTo`, or left uncategorised when `force` was used. 409 when the category still holds topics and neither parameter was given.

topics.description: Topics that were moved or uncategorised.

movedTo.description: The category they were re-filed under, if any.

get.summary: The inbound email address for a forum space

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 100. 500 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Where to continue from: pass back the `page.nextCursor` of the previous answer. Opaque — there is nothing inside one to construct or parse. Sending one also opts into the enveloped shape, exactly as stating `Forumulate-Version` does.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

oneOf.description: The block-JSON form of this body. Send `content` and no `markdown`; sending both is a 422.

markdown.description: The body as Markdown (CommonMark + tables/task lists), converted server-side. Alternative to `content`. Blocks beyond plain Markdown (callouts, tabs, cards, steppers, columns, buttons, …) are written as `:::name{attrs}` directives — every directive, its attributes and how it closes: `GET /docs/markdown-dialect`. Up to 2,000,000 characters of Markdown — the same ceiling the importer, the create and the update doors all use, so an imported page can always be written back.

oneOf.description: The Markdown form of the same body, converted server-side into the same blocks. Send `markdown` and no `content`; sending both is a 422.

schema.description: `content` and `markdown` are ALTERNATIVES: send one of them. `markdown` is converted into the same block document `content` carries, so the resource that comes back is identical either way. Sending both is a 422 — nothing silently wins, because a client that sent the wrong field would otherwise see a 201 and the wrong body.

409.description: Refused because of the state this already is in — a name or slug already taken, a resource that already exists, or a precondition on the thing itself (`conflict`, `*.taken`, `*.exists`). Unlike a 422 the body is fine; unlike a 503 retrying it unchanged will not help.

429.description: Rate limited — see the RateLimit-* headers.

customCss.description: CSS for THIS piece only, after the space theme so it wins. Sanitised and scoped to the reader exactly like the space `customCss` (`@import` dropped, no way out of the <style>).

theme.description: A partial theme for this piece — colours, palettes, fonts, typography, colorScheme, components, contentWidth, layout, motion, and (on a blog post) `post` — layered over the space’s (which is over the site’s). On a post, release, event or legal document `PATCH` it MERGES key by key like the space theme’s PATCH, and `null` clears at any depth (`{"paletteDark": null}`); a page’s metadata replaces it whole. Unknown keys are refused by name. `null` clears all of it.

shareImageUrl.description: The og:image / twitter:image for this piece, separate from its cover. Wins over the cover and over the generated social card.

jsonLd.description: Structured data for this piece, as JSON (object or array of objects). Replaces the automatic markup on this piece (Article/BlogPosting, Event, DiscussionForumPosting/QAPage, the roadmap item’s Article). `null` restores the automatic one.

customization.description: This piece’s own look and share card: `customCss`, `theme` (partial), `shareImageUrl`, `ogTitle`, `ogDescription`, `twitterCard`, `jsonLd`. Keys merge on write; `null` clears one key, or every key when sent for the whole object.

oneOf.description: The block-JSON form of this body. Send `content` and no `markdown`; sending both is a 422.

markdown.description: The body as Markdown (CommonMark + tables/task lists), converted server-side. Alternative to `content`. Blocks beyond plain Markdown (callouts, tabs, cards, steppers, columns, buttons, …) are written as `:::name{attrs}` directives — every directive, its attributes and how it closes: `GET /docs/markdown-dialect`. Up to 2,000,000 characters of Markdown — the same ceiling the importer, the create and the update doors all use, so an imported page can always be written back.

Unknown keys are refused by name. `null` clears all of it.

shareImageUrl.description: The og:image / twitter:image for this piece, separate from its cover. Wins over the cover and over the generated social card.

jsonLd.description: Structured data for this piece, as JSON (object or array of objects). Replaces the automatic markup on this piece (Article/BlogPosting, Event, DiscussionForumPosting/QAPage, the roadmap item’s Article). `null` restores the automatic one.

customization.description: This piece’s own look and share card: `customCss`, `theme` (partial), `shareImageUrl`, `ogTitle`, `ogDescription`, `twitterCard`, `jsonLd`. Keys merge on write; `null` clears one key, or every key when sent for the whole object.

oneOf.description: The Markdown form of the same body, converted server-side into the same blocks. Send `markdown` and no `content`; sending both is a 422.

schema.description: `content` and `markdown` are ALTERNATIVES: send one of them. `markdown` is converted into the same block document `content` carries, so the resource that comes back is identical either way. Sending both is a 422 — nothing silently wins, because a client that sent the wrong field would otherwise see a 201 and the wrong body.

oneOf.description: The block-JSON form of this body. Send `content` and no `markdown`; sending both is a 422.

markdown.description: The body as Markdown (CommonMark + tables/task lists), converted server-side. Alternative to `content`. Blocks beyond plain Markdown (callouts, tabs, cards, steppers, columns, buttons, …) are written as `:::name{attrs}` directives — every directive, its attributes and how it closes: `GET /docs/markdown-dialect`. Up to 2,000,000 characters of Markdown — the same ceiling the importer, the create and the update doors all use, so an imported page can always be written back.

oneOf.description: The Markdown form of the same body, converted server-side into the same blocks. Send `markdown` and no `content`; sending both is a 422.

schema.description: `content` and `markdown` are ALTERNATIVES: send one of them. `markdown` is converted into the same block document `content` carries, so the resource that comes back is identical either way. Sending both is a 422 — nothing silently wins, because a client that sent the wrong field would otherwise see a 201 and the wrong body.

parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 100. 500 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.description: Which page of results to return, 1-based. Out-of-range pages return an empty list.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page — the spelling used everywhere else in this API. This endpoint also accepts `pageSize`, which it has always taken; `limit` wins if both are sent. Defaults to 25. 100 is the most it serves — a larger value is capped, not refused, and a value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422.

anyOf.description: This is the pre-envelope shape, served only to callers who state no `forumulate-version`. It stops being served on 2027-09-01 — the same date this operation's `Sunset` response header carries. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to get the `page` envelope instead, which is the variant beside this one.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

get.summary: Get the search in a space (public reader forum)

get.description: Operators: category:<slug>, tag:<t>, tags:a,b, -tag:<t>, status:solved|unsolved|open|closed|archived|noreplies, in:title|pinned|tagged|untagged (plus in:bookmarks|watching|tracking|muted|seen|unseen when signed in), @author, before:/after:YYYY-MM-DD, created:, order:latest|top|views|latest_topic, min_views:, min_posts:. `total` counts the whole matched set; `hits` is one page of it.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Hits per page. Defaults to 20. 50 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Hits skipped. Defaults to 0. 1000 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 0 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

200.description:
Success.

This answer carries no `page` object: the forum's operator search (F-162): ranked per request like the unified search above, so it publishes `offset` into a ranking and `total` for the matched set rather than a cursor into a collection. `?limit=` caps how much of the ranking you get; there is no cursor to walk, and `hasMore` would have nothing true to say.

oneOf.description: The block-JSON form of this body. Send `content` and no `markdown`; sending both is a 422.

markdown.description: The body as Markdown (CommonMark + tables/task lists), converted server-side. Alternative to `content`. Blocks beyond plain Markdown (callouts, tabs, cards, steppers, columns, buttons, …) are written as `:::name{attrs}` directives — every directive, its attributes and how it closes: `GET /docs/markdown-dialect`. Up to 2,000,000 characters of Markdown — the same ceiling the importer, the create and the update doors all use, so an imported page can always be written back.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.
