parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Members on the board. Defaults to 25. 100 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

200.description:
Members ranked by the source’s value, highest first. The array is `leaders` — published without a response schema until now, which left integrators guessing between `leaders`, `standings` and `entries`.

This answer carries no `page` object: top N by an external score; the ranking is recomputed per request, so there is no row to resume after. `?limit=` caps how much of the ranking you get; there is no cursor to walk, and `hasMore` would have nothing true to say.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Members per page. Defaults to 25. 100 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Which page of results to return, 1-based. Out-of-range pages return an empty list.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page — the spelling used everywhere else in this API. This endpoint also accepts `pageSize`, which it has always taken; `limit` wins if both are sent. anyOf.description: This is the pre-envelope shape, served only to callers who state no `forumulate-version`. It stops being served on 2027-09-01 — the same date this operation's `Sunset` response header carries. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to get the `page` envelope instead, which is the variant beside this one.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

400.description: The request could not be understood — a malformed header, path or query value (`request.malformed`). A value that was understood but is not acceptable is a 422 `validation.failed`.

401.description: No credential, or one that is expired or revoked (`auth.required`). Send a Bearer token or the session cookie.

403.description: Authenticated, and not allowed — always `rbac.forbidden`, whether what is missing is the capability, the token scope, or a resource the token is pinned away from. The message names the capability and, for a scope refusal, the scopes that would grant it. A refusal because of the PLAN is a 402 with `quota.exceeded`, not this.

404.description: No such thing — one of the ids in the path does not resolve, or resolves to something this caller may not see (`*.not_found`).

429.description: Rate limited — see the RateLimit-* headers.

default.description: Error — the stable { error: { code, message } } envelope.

get.description: **Requires token scope: `read`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

data.description: The created resource again, under a key that is the same on every create — so a generic client needs one parser rather than one per endpoint. It is the SAME object as the key named after the resource (`page`, `article`, `topic`, …), which remains the canonical name.

warnings.description: Values we ACCEPTED and then rewrote, one sentence each — a slugified tag, a normalised colour, a clamped range, a slug that was taken. **Absent when nothing was rewritten**, never `[]`. The same sentences are on the `X-Field-Warnings` response header. If this is present, something you sent is not what is stored; read the resource back rather than assuming your own value.

oneOf.description: The block-JSON form of this body. Send `content` and no `markdown`; sending both is a 422.

markdown.description: The body as Markdown (CommonMark + tables/task lists), converted server-side. Alternative to `content`. Blocks beyond plain Markdown (callouts, tabs, cards, steppers, columns, buttons, …) are written as `:::name{attrs}` directives — every directive, its attributes and how it closes: `GET /docs/markdown-dialect`. Up to 2,000,000 characters of Markdown — the same ceiling the importer, the create and the update doors all use, so an imported page can always be written back.

oneOf.description: The Markdown form of the same body, converted server-side into the same blocks. Send `markdown` and no `content`; sending both is a 422.

schema.description: `content` and `markdown` are ALTERNATIVES: send one of them. `markdown` is converted into the same block document `content` carries, so the resource that comes back is identical either way. Sending both is a 422 — nothing silently wins, because a client that sent the wrong field would otherwise see a 201 and the wrong body.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 100. 500 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

200.description:
Success.

This answer carries no `page` object: the in-app widget's newest releases (at most 30) for THIS visitor's segment, the boosted one pinned first — re-chosen per visitor, so there is no stable set to resume; the changelog itself is the paged collection. `?limit=` caps how much of the ranking you get; there is no cursor to walk, and `hasMore` would have nothing true to say.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Events per page, once a version is stated. Defaults to 100. 500 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.name: from

anyOf.description: This is the pre-envelope shape, served only to callers who state no `forumulate-version`. It stops being served on 2027-09-01 — the same date this operation's `Sunset` response header carries. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to get the `page` envelope instead, which is the variant beside this one.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

400.description: The request could not be understood — a malformed header, path or query value (`request.malformed`). A value that was understood but is not acceptable is a 422 `validation.failed`.

401.description: No credential, or one that is expired or revoked (`auth.required`). Send a Bearer token or the session cookie.

403.description: Authenticated, and not allowed — always `rbac.forbidden`, whether what is missing is the capability, the token scope, or a resource the token is pinned away from. The message names the capability and, for a scope refusal, the scopes that would grant it. A refusal because of the PLAN is a 402 with `quota.exceeded`, not this.

404.description: No such thing — one of the ids in the path does not resolve, or resolves to something this caller may not see (`*.not_found`).

429.description: Rate limited — see the RateLimit-* headers.

default.description: Error — the stable { error: { code, message } } envelope.

get.description:
The events a member can see in this space, upcoming or all. The read behind a public calendar or an "what is on" block; drafts are excluded unless the caller may manage them.

**Requires token scope: `read`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

data.description: The created resource again, under a key that is the same on every create — so a generic client needs one parser rather than one per endpoint. It is the SAME object as the key named after the resource (`page`, `article`, `topic`, …), which remains the canonical name.

warnings.description: Values we ACCEPTED and then rewrote, one sentence each — a slugified tag, a normalised colour, a clamped range, a slug that was taken. **Absent when nothing was rewritten**, never `[]`. The same sentences are on the `X-Field-Warnings` response header. If this is present, something you sent is not what is stored; read the resource back rather than assuming your own value.

400.description: The request could not be understood — a malformed header, path or query value (`request.malformed`). A value that was understood but is not acceptable is a 422 `validation.failed`.

401.description: No credential, or one that is expired or revoked (`auth.required`). Send a Bearer token or the session cookie.

403.description: Authenticated, and not allowed — always `rbac.forbidden`, whether what is missing is the capability, the token scope, or a resource the token is pinned away from. The message names the capability and, for a scope refusal, the scopes that would grant it. A refusal because of the PLAN is a 402 with `quota.exceeded`, not this.

404.description: No such thing — one of the ids in the path does not resolve, or resolves to something this caller may not see (`*.not_found`).

422.description: The body was understood and a value is unacceptable (`validation.failed`). `error.details` names the field paths.

429.description: Rate limited — see the RateLimit-* headers.

default.description: Error — the stable { error: { code, message } } envelope.

timezone.description: IANA time-zone name the event is published in, e.g. Europe/Berlin.

coverAlt.description: What the cover shows, for screen readers and link previews.

stateReason.description: Why it was cancelled or postponed — shown in the banner on the event page.

joinLinkVisibility.description: `public` (default) or `attendees`: only readers who RSVP `going` get the join link.

tags.description: Tag slugs. Labels and colours come from the space’s tag registry, like a blog’s.

hosts.description: Who hosts it, in order: `{name, role?, url?, avatarUrl?}` or `{author: <key>}` from the space’s author registry (`…/spaces/{spaceId}/authors`).

customCss.description: CSS for THIS piece only, after the space theme so it wins. Sanitised and scoped to the reader exactly like the space `customCss` (`@import` dropped, no way out of the <style>).

theme.description: A partial theme for this piece — colours, palettes, fonts, typography, colorScheme, components, contentWidth, layout, motion, and (on a blog post) `post` — layered over the space’s (which is over the site’s). On a post, release, event or legal document `PATCH` it MERGES key by key like the space theme’s PATCH, and `null` clears at any depth (`{"paletteDark": null}`); a page’s metadata replaces it whole. Unknown keys are refused by name. `null` clears all of it.

shareImageUrl.description: The og:image / twitter:image for this piece, separate from its cover. Wins over the cover and over the generated social card.

jsonLd.description: Structured data for this piece, as JSON (object or array of objects). Replaces the automatic markup on this piece (Article/BlogPosting, Event, DiscussionForumPosting/QAPage, the roadmap item’s Article). `null` restores the automatic one.

rsvpApproval.description: A `going` waits as `pending` until staff approve it. Default false.

guestsMax.description: How many guests (+1s) one RSVP may bring. Default 0.

questions.description: Registration questions (the Forms field model), answered when RSVPing `going`.

recurrence.description: Repeat this event: `{freq: daily|weekly|monthly, interval?, byWeekday?, count?, until?}`. Each later date becomes its own event (own RSVPs) in the series; `null` stops the series. Only on an event that is not itself a generated date.

seriesScope.description: On a series’ first event: `following` also applies this change to every date still to come. Default `this`.

gallery.description: Photos from the event, shown on its page once it is over.

recapUrl.description: The write-up: a blog post (a path on this site or a URL), linked once it is over.

feedbackFormId.description: A form of this organization (Forms) asked of readers once the event is over.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

parameters.name: limit

200.description: A grounded answer, streamed. Frames are NAMED (`token`, `citations`, `done`, `error`), so subscribe per event rather than with `onmessage`. Prose arrives token by token; the `citations` frame carries the anchor-level sources for what was just said; `done` carries the `queryId` to rate the answer with. An error after the first token arrives as an `error` FRAME, not as a status — the status is already committed — and the client falls back to the blocking `docs/ask`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 100. 500 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Where to continue from: pass back the `page.nextCursor` of the previous answer. Opaque — there is nothing inside one to construct or parse. Sending one also opts into the enveloped shape, exactly as stating `Forumulate-Version` does.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

get.description:
A collection table for people: draft values with status, lock and “used in” beside each row, filtered with the same `where` a preview key sends — so a filter built here can be copied into a site’s code and answers the same rows.

The collection table: draft values (as a preview key reads them), filtered by `where`, ordered by `sort` and walked by `cursor` with the delivery grammar — so the same query sent to `GET /delivery/v1/libraries/{libraryId}/types/{type}/entries` with a preview key answers the same rows. Each row adds its title, status (`draft`, `changed`, `scheduled`, `published`), who is editing it and how many entries reference it. `locale` picks the locale; references are not populated unless `depth` is given.

**Requires token scope: `read`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: `{field: {operator: value}}` with `and`/`or` lists, as JSON or bracket-encoded (`where[price][gt]=10`). Operators: equals, not_equals, in, not_in, contains, like, exists, gt, gte, lt, lte, near.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated field paths, `-` first for descending. Default: the type’s `defaultSort`, else `-updatedAt`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Entries per window, 1–100 (default 20; above 100 is capped).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `page.nextCursor` from the previous window. A cursor from a different sort is a 422.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Ask for `page.total`; sent only where counting is cheap.

post.description:
Acts on a whole selection in one request — publish fifty, unpublish, trash, or copy into a locale — and reports each entry on its own, so three refusals never undo forty-seven successes.

Applies one action to up to 100 entries in one request. Each entry goes through the same checks its single-entry route makes (a strict type refuses empty required fields; a referenced entry is not deleted without `force`), and each is reported on its own in `results`, in the order named, with the status, code and reason it would have answered alone. Entries that are not in this library are reported 404. `localeCopy` gives each entry a draft twin in `locale` seeded from the source; existing twins are kept unless `overwrite`.

**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

post.summary: Publish, unpublish, delete or copy many entries

action.description: `publish` makes each draft live; `unpublish` takes each out of delivery and keeps it as a draft; `delete` moves each to the trash (30 days); `localeCopy` gives each entry a twin in `locale` seeded with the source values.

entryIds.description: The entries, at most 100. Each is reported on its own.

locale.description: `localeCopy`: the library locale to copy into (a BCP-47 code the library has).

overwrite.description: `localeCopy`: also replace the localized values of twins that already exist. Default false: an existing twin is left as a translator left it.

force.description: `delete`: delete even entries other entries reference (their references then resolve to null).

get.description:

A key still inside a rotation’s overlap shows `retiresAt`. Secrets are never listed. Last use and counts are folded in by a once-a-minute sweep.

get.description: One window of a content type’s entries in one locale, filtered by `where`, ordered by `sort` and walked by cursor (`page.nextCursor` while `page.hasMore`). References are populated to `depth`. A `where` or `sort` on a field that is not indexed is served only on a small type; past that it is a 422 naming the field to index. Locales: a list holds ONE row per entry, read through the fallback chain like a one-entry read: the entry’s twin in `locale` when it has one, otherwise its twin in the first chain locale that has one, otherwise the source. With `fallback=false` only entries that have a twin in `locale` are listed. `where` and `sort` read the listed twin’s OWN localized values (a localized field that twin left empty — filled in the response from the rest of the chain — matches as absent and sorts as missing) and the source entry’s non-localized values. Each row’s `locale` says which twin was listed; `count=true` counts the same rows.

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: `{field: {operator: value}}` with `and`/`or` lists, as JSON or bracket-encoded (`where[price][gt]=10`). Operators: equals, not_equals, in, not_in, contains, like, exists, gt, gte, lt, lte, near.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated field paths, `-` first for descending. Default: the type’s `defaultSort`, else `-updatedAt`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Entries per window, 1–100 (default 20; above 100 is capped).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `page.nextCursor` from the previous window. A cursor from a different sort is a 422.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Ask for `page.total`; sent only where counting is cheap.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: A locale code (the library’s source locale when omitted). `*` on a one-entry or global read returns every locale under `localized`.

parameters.name: fallback
parameters.description: Fall back through the declared locale chain, then the source (default `true`). Whole entry: a locale with no twin serves the first twin of its chain. Per field: an empty localized field — and an empty localized leaf inside a localized group, array or blocks row, matched by row id — is filled from the first entry of the chain that has it. Non-localized fields always come from the source entry. `false`: only the asked locale, empty fields left empty.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: How far references are populated: 0 serves stubs `{kind, id, contentType, slug}`. Default 1; capped by the plan’s reference depth (a larger value is a 422).

parameters.name: populate
parameters.description: Per type, the fields to keep on a populated entry: `populate[author]=name,avatar`.

parameters.name: select
parameters.description: Comma-separated field paths to keep in `fields`.

parameters.name: draft
parameters.description: Accepted for a preview key, which always reads drafts; a delivery key asking for drafts is a 403.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

Every piece in a space under one shape, whatever the space’s type calls them — articles, topics, releases, roadmap cards, pages. The endpoint to build a cross-type integration against instead of learning six per-type doors. Each row carries `locale`, the language declared for that piece (never the space default), and an `id` that is the same value its kind’s own routes use — a page item’s id is its `GET …/pages` id.

parameters.description: The tag you believe this resource is at: the `ETag` header the matching read sets. It is opaque and changes on any change to the resource (body, title, slug, `locale`, metadata). The `contentHash` that read returned is also accepted and guards the content only — it does not move on a metadata edit. The write is applied only if the tag still holds, so two editors cannot overwrite each other unnoticed. A list is accepted and any member matching is enough; `*` asserts only that the resource exists. Omit it and the write is unconditional. On every other route a concrete value is a 428 rather than silently ignored.

An `http` check is UP when the request connected AND the response status is below 400 (2xx and 3xx both pass); a `keyword` additionally requires that term in the body, and `certExpiryDays` requires that many days left on the TLS certificate. Set `expectStatus` (100-599) and that EXACT code becomes the only status that counts as up — anything else, 200 included, is down — which is how you watch a dependency whose healthy unauthenticated answer is a 401 or a 405. Null (the default) keeps the under-400 rule. Like `keyword` and `certExpiryDays`, it applies to `http` checks only — a `heartbeat` monitor has no response to inspect and is UP while the job has pinged within `intervalSeconds`.

autoStart.description: Maintenance: move to in progress at `scheduledFor` (default true). Subscribers are told.

autoComplete.description: Maintenance: complete at `scheduledUntil` (default true). Off, it stays in progress until you complete it — for work you verify by hand.

get.description: `overall` and each component's `status` are the REPORTED state, and three things decide it, in this order: a human's `declaredState` always wins; then the latest check (a failing one is a `major_outage`); then measured history is allowed to degrade a passing check — under 99.5% uptime reads `degraded` and under 97% reads `partial_outage`, so the headline can no longer contradict the percentage printed beside it. History only ever degrades, never improves, and only once `window.sufficient` is true (at least 20 checks spanning at least 6 hours). `window` says what each percentage was actually measured over — `samples`, `daysCovered`, `spanHours` and the first/last check — because `uptime` alone was being printed beside a hardcoded '90 days'. `historyDays` are the day keys the `history` arrays line up with, oldest first. `outages` are the failing runs our own checks recorded, longer than each monitor's `failureThreshold`, whether or not anybody opened an incident for them.

get.description: statuspage.io's `summary.json` shape, derived from the same board a person reads so the two cannot disagree. Components keep OUR state words (`degraded`, `maintenance`, `unknown`) and carry Statuspage's `id`, `description`, `position`, `group_id` (plus `group_name` and `slug`); `incidents` are the open ones with `id`, `impact`, `shortlink` and `incident_updates`; `scheduled_maintenances` lists maintenance not yet over; `page` has `id`, `time_zone` and `updated_at`. The Statuspage-worded twin is `…/status/api/v2/summary.json`. `uptime` is nullable (null means nothing was recorded, which is NOT 0%) and each component carries the `window` its percentage was measured over, so a poller can tell '100% over ninety days' from '100% over ninety minutes'. `outages` lists the failing runs our own checks recorded even when no incident was opened. The snake_case keys inside `incidents` are deliberate Statuspage compatibility, not our envelope drifting.

post.description:
`{ "value": 12.5 }` for one point now, `{ "value": 12.5, "at": "<ISO>" }` for one point then, or `{ "points": [...] }` for up to 500. The first push to a key that does not exist creates the metric, visible and named by its key. post.description: A heartbeat from a scheduled job saying it ran: the signed URL is the whole credential, so a cron line or a CI step can call it with nothing else. Wire it into the job itself — a monitor that has never been pinged reports unknown rather than down. A run that partly failed can say so with `{"ok": false, "detail": "…"}` instead of going silent.

403.description: Authenticated, and not allowed — always `rbac.forbidden`, whether what is missing is the capability, the token scope, or a resource the token is pinned away from. The message names the capability and, for a scope refusal, the scopes that would grant it. A refusal because of the PLAN is a 402 with `quota.exceeded`, not this.

422.description: The body was understood and a value is unacceptable (`validation.failed`). `error.details` names the field paths.

429.description: Rate limited — see the RateLimit-* headers.

default.description: Error — the stable { error: { code, message } } envelope.

put.description: **Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Which page shape to apply. A shape adds named slots to what a piece of this space is made of; it is NOT the reader layout (that is `PUT …/preset`). `how-to` — One task, done. The goal, what you need first, the steps, and how to tell it worked. `tutorial` — Learning by building something end to end — for somebody who does not know the product yet. `reference` — What something is and exactly how it behaves — read in a hurry, by somebody who already knows why. `explanation` — Why something works the way it does — the page that stops the same question being asked forever. `troubleshooting` — One symptom, its cause, and the fix — written for somebody who is already annoyed. `bug-report` — What happened, what should have happened, and how to see it — the three things a fix needs. `feature-request` — The problem first, then the idea — so somebody can solve it a better way than you asked for. `question` — Asks for the context, what was already tried, and what was expected — the three things a good answer needs. `landing` — A wide opening statement, then the three things you want somebody to do next. `comparison` — Two things, side by side, and the honest sentence about when to pick each. `release` — What shipped, what it changes for a reader, and what to do if it broke something. `keepachangelog` — The standard changelog categories — Added, Changed, Fixed, and the rest — one list each. `incident` — What broke, who it hit, what you did, and what stops it happening again. `role` — The work, who it suits, what it pays, and how to apply. `policy` — A plain-English summary over the document itself, so somebody can read either. `announcement` — One thing, said properly: what it is, why now, and what a reader does about it. `faq-answer` — The answer first, then the reason, for the question you keep being asked.

post.summary: Create a submission in a space
post.description: Sends a contact space's form from a `contactForm` block on any page, as flat pairs (the built-in name/email/subject/body/department plus each question by its own name). The same pipeline as the contact page — routing, topic questions, inbox, mail, webhook — and the same two answers as the forms door: JSON, or a 303 for a plain HTML post.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 100. 500 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Where to continue from: pass back the `page.nextCursor` of the previous answer. Opaque — there is nothing inside one to construct or parse. Sending one also opts into the enveloped shape, exactly as stating `Forumulate-Version` does.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

parameters.name: cursor

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

Link.description: Carries `rel="deprecation"` pointing at <https://forumulate.com/reference/versioning> when the two headers above are present, appended to whatever other links the response already had.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`, because only then are you served the pre-envelope shape. It is a Structured-Field **Date** — an `@` and Unix seconds, never `true` — and it is the day that shape became deprecated (`2026-09-01`), not the day it is withdrawn. For that, read `Sunset`.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only when you state no `forumulate-version`. The date the pre-envelope response shape stops being served: **2027-09-01**. The ROUTE is not going away and neither are its path, its parameters or its errors — after this date a request that states no version simply receives the `2026-09-01` shape. Send `forumulate-version: 2026-09-01` to move now and the header stops arriving.

enabled.description: `false` hides the switcher (the same as `placement: "none"`). Unset: shown.

placement.description: Where the content-language switcher sits: header (the nav bar's end) | header-start | header-overflow (the header menu) | sidebar | footer | content-top | floating | none. Unset: the surface’s own place (docs: sidebar; others: content-top).

style.description: `select` (unset): the reader dropdown, from the control tokens. `pills`: a row of links. `compact`: a tight row of codes (EN · ES).

names.description: How each language is named: native (unset, "Español"), english ("Spanish"), code ("ES").

flags.description: A flag before each name. Off by default.

flagCountries.description: The country whose flag stands for a language: `{ "en": "US", "pt-BR": "BR" }`.

locales.description: Which languages are listed, in order (codes; `default` = the original). Unset: all declared.

customLabels.description: A label per language code (`default` = the original), over `names`.

missing.description: When this page has no translation in a language: home (unset — that language’s front door), disabled (listed, not a link), hide (only languages this page is translated into).

remember.description: Keep the reader’s pick, so a page in another language offers its translation. Never changes a page’s own language. Off by default.

customCss.description: CSS for THIS piece only, after the space theme so it wins. Sanitised and scoped to the reader exactly like the space `customCss` (`@import` dropped, no way out of the <style>).

theme.description: A partial theme for this piece — colours, palettes, fonts, typography, colorScheme, components, contentWidth, layout, motion, and (on a blog post) `post` — layered over the space’s (which is over the site’s). On a post, release, event or legal document `PATCH` it MERGES key by key like the space theme’s PATCH, and `null` clears at any depth (`{"paletteDark": null}`); a page’s metadata replaces it whole. Unknown keys are refused by name. `null` clears all of it.

shareImageUrl.description: The og:image / twitter:image for this piece, separate from its cover. Wins over the cover and over the generated social card.

jsonLd.description: Structured data for this piece, as JSON (object or array of objects). Replaces the automatic markup on this piece (Article/BlogPosting, Event, DiscussionForumPosting/QAPage, the roadmap item’s Article). `null` restores the automatic one.

enabled.description: `false` hides the switcher (the same as `placement: "none"`). Unset: shown.

placement.description: Where the content-language switcher sits: header (the nav bar's end) | header-start | header-overflow (the header menu) | sidebar | footer | content-top | floating | none. Unset: the surface’s own place (docs: sidebar; others: content-top).

style.description: `select` (unset): the reader dropdown, from the control tokens. `pills`: a row of links. `compact`: a tight row of codes (EN · ES).

names.description: How each language is named: native (unset, "Español"), english ("Spanish"), code ("ES").

flags.description: A flag before each name. Off by default.

flagCountries.description: The country whose flag stands for a language: `{ "en": "US", "pt-BR": "BR" }`.

locales.description: Which languages are listed, in order (codes; `default` = the original). Unset: all declared.

customLabels.description: A label per language code (`default` = the original), over `names`.

missing.description: When this page has no translation in a language: home (unset — that language’s front door), disabled (listed, not a link), hide (only languages this page is translated into).

remember.description: Keep the reader’s pick, so a page in another language offers its translation. Never changes a page’s own language. Off by default.

customCss.description: CSS for THIS piece only, after the space theme so it wins. Sanitised and scoped to the reader exactly like the space `customCss` (`@import` dropped, no way out of the <style>).

theme.description: A partial theme for this piece — colours, palettes, fonts, typography, colorScheme, components, contentWidth, layout, motion, and (on a blog post) `post` — layered over the space’s (which is over the site’s). On a post, release, event or legal document `PATCH` it MERGES key by key like the space theme’s PATCH, and `null` clears at any depth (`{"paletteDark": null}`); a page’s metadata replaces it whole. Unknown keys are refused by name. `null` clears all of it.

shareImageUrl.description: The og:image / twitter:image for this piece, separate from its cover. Wins over the cover and over the generated social card.

jsonLd.description: Structured data for this piece, as JSON (object or array of objects). Replaces the automatic markup on this piece (Article/BlogPosting, Event, DiscussionForumPosting/QAPage, the roadmap item’s Article). `null` restores the automatic one.

parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 100. 500 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.description: Where to continue from: pass back the `page.nextCursor` of the previous answer. Opaque — there is nothing inside one to construct or parse. Sending one also opts into the enveloped shape, exactly as stating `Forumulate-Version` does.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

enabled.description: `false` hides the switcher (the same as `placement: "none"`). Unset: shown.

placement.description: Where the content-language switcher sits: header (the nav bar's end) | header-start | header-overflow (the header menu) | sidebar | footer | content-top | floating | none. Unset: the surface’s own place (docs: sidebar; others: content-top).

style.description: `select` (unset): the reader dropdown, from the control tokens. `pills`: a row of links. `compact`: a tight row of codes (EN · ES).

names.description: How each language is named: native (unset, "Español"), english ("Spanish"), code ("ES").

flags.description: A flag before each name. Off by default.

flagCountries.description: The country whose flag stands for a language: `{ "en": "US", "pt-BR": "BR" }`.

locales.description: Which languages are listed, in order (codes; `default` = the original). Unset: all declared.

customLabels.description: A label per language code (`default` = the original), over `names`.

missing.description: When this page has no translation in a language: home (unset — that language’s front door), disabled (listed, not a link), hide (only languages this page is translated into).

remember.description: Keep the reader’s pick, so a page in another language offers its translation. Never changes a page’s own language. Off by default.

customCss.description: CSS for THIS piece only, after the space theme so it wins. Sanitised and scoped to the reader exactly like the space `customCss` (`@import` dropped, no way out of the <style>).

theme.description: A partial theme for this piece — colours, palettes, fonts, typography, colorScheme, components, contentWidth, layout, motion, and (on a blog post) `post` — layered over the space’s (which is over the site’s). On a post, release, event or legal document `PATCH` it MERGES key by key like the space theme’s PATCH, and `null` clears at any depth (`{"paletteDark": null}`); a page’s metadata replaces it whole. Unknown keys are refused by name. `null` clears all of it.

shareImageUrl.description: The og:image / twitter:image for this piece, separate from its cover. Wins over the cover and over the generated social card.

jsonLd.description: Structured data for this piece, as JSON (object or array of objects). Replaces the automatic markup on this piece (Article/BlogPosting, Event, DiscussionForumPosting/QAPage, the roadmap item’s Article). `null` restores the automatic one.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 100. 500 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Where to continue from: pass back the `page.nextCursor` of the previous answer. Opaque — there is nothing inside one to construct or parse. Sending one also opts into the enveloped shape, exactly as stating `Forumulate-Version` does.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 100. 500 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Where to continue from: pass back the `page.nextCursor` of the previous answer. Opaque — there is nothing inside one to construct or parse. Sending one also opts into the enveloped shape, exactly as stating `Forumulate-Version` does.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The tag you believe this resource is at: the `ETag` header the matching read sets. It is opaque and changes on any change to the resource (body, title, slug, `locale`, metadata). The `contentHash` that read returned is also accepted and guards the content only — it does not move on a metadata edit. The write is applied only if the tag still holds, so two editors cannot overwrite each other unnoticed. A list is accepted and any member matching is enough; `*` asserts only that the resource exists. Omit it and the write is unconditional. On every other route a concrete value is a 428 rather than silently ignored.

get.description: The current published text of one document by its role — terms, privacy, cookies. Fetch by role rather than by id, so the footer keeps working after a new edition replaces the old one. `?locale=<code>` serves its translation twin in one of the space's declared languages; `locale` names the language served and `locales` lists the declared ones.

The reader surface renders the acceptance step from this. `documents` is empty when nothing is pending. `acceptor` is null when there is nobody to record an acceptance against — under the default (`require_identity`) that means the reader must sign in first, which is why a `read` gate cannot be configured on a space with no reader sign-in. The reader's subject itself is never returned: it can be an address a host app signed into a JWT, and this endpoint is anonymous.

parameters.name: orgId
parameters.description: The organization: its uuid, or the name in its `slug`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 100. 500 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Where to continue from: pass back the `page.nextCursor` of the previous answer. Opaque — there is nothing inside one to construct or parse. Sending one also opts into the enveloped shape, exactly as stating `Forumulate-Version` does.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 100. 500 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Where to continue from: pass back the `page.nextCursor` of the previous answer. Opaque — there is nothing inside one to construct or parse. Sending one also opts into the enveloped shape, exactly as stating `Forumulate-Version` does.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

enabled.description: `false` hides the switcher (the same as `placement: "none"`). Unset: shown.

placement.description: Where the content-language switcher sits: header (the nav bar's end) | header-start | header-overflow (the header menu) | sidebar | footer | content-top | floating | none. Unset: the surface’s own place (docs: sidebar; others: content-top).

style.description: `select` (unset): the reader dropdown, from the control tokens. `pills`: a row of links. `compact`: a tight row of codes (EN · ES).

names.description: How each language is named: native (unset, "Español"), english ("Spanish"), code ("ES").

flags.description: A flag before each name. Off by default.

flagCountries.description: The country whose flag stands for a language: `{ "en": "US", "pt-BR": "BR" }`.

locales.description: Which languages are listed, in order (codes; `default` = the original). Unset: all declared.

customLabels.description: A label per language code (`default` = the original), over `names`.

missing.description: When this page has no translation in a language: home (unset — that language’s front door), disabled (listed, not a link), hide (only languages this page is translated into).

remember.description: Keep the reader’s pick, so a page in another language offers its translation. Never changes a page’s own language. Off by default.

path.description: Where the page answers on the site: `/` for the root, or one segment (`/pricing`).

spaceId.description: The member space the page belongs to.

page.description: The page, by its slug in that space.

pageMounts.description: Single pages published at a path of the site: `{ path: "/pricing", spaceId, page: "<slug>" }`, or `path: "/"` to make one page the site root instead of the generated index. The space must be a member, the page must exist, and a path may not shadow a member space’s own segment. The page’s address inside its space redirects (308) to the mounted path, which is its canonical.

post.description:
Gathers public spaces under one address so they share a header, a footer and a theme instead of keeping a copy of the design each. The membership list is optional — an empty site is the normal first move, because later public spaces join the oldest one by themselves.

**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

400.description: The request could not be understood — a malformed header, path or query value (`request.malformed`). A value that was understood but is not acceptable is a 422 `validation.failed`.

401.description: No credential, or one that is expired or revoked (`auth.required`). Send a Bearer token or the session cookie.

403.description: Authenticated, and not allowed — always `rbac.forbidden`, whether what is missing is the capability, the token scope, or a resource the token is pinned away from. The message names the capability and, for a scope refusal, the scopes that would grant it. A refusal because of the PLAN is a 402 with `quota.exceeded`, not this.

404.description: No such thing — one of the ids in the path does not resolve, or resolves to something this caller may not see (`*.not_found`).

429.description: Rate limited — see the RateLimit-* headers.

default.description: Error — the stable { error: { code, message } } envelope.

get.description:
One site with everything stored on it, which is the read half of any change you make: fetch, alter the branch you care about, send that branch back. Also how you confirm what a write really left behind, rather than trusting the echo of what you sent.

**Requires token scope: `read`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Use true or false (true/1/yes/on and false/0/no/off are accepted).

warnings.description: Values we ACCEPTED and then rewrote, one sentence each — a slugified tag, a normalised colour, a clamped range, a slug that was taken. **Absent when nothing was rewritten**, never `[]`. The same sentences are on the `X-Field-Warnings` response header. If this is present, something you sent is not what is stored; read the resource back rather than assuming your own value.

config.description: DEEP-MERGED onto the stored config: nested objects merge, arrays and scalars replace. A key you leave out is KEPT — send it as `null` to delete it (`{"footer":{"art":null}}`), or use `PUT` to replace the whole config. Header and footer keys (`cta`, `headerLinks`, `footerColumns`, `footer`, `socialLinks`, …) sit at the TOP of `config`, never under `config.theme.chrome` (a 422). Inside a site, the site’s chrome and `config.theme.whiteLabel` win over each member space’s own. `?dryRun=true` answers the diff and writes nothing.

config.footerDescription: How to install the SDK and make your first call.

patch.description:
Deep-merges into the stored configuration, so renaming the call-to-action cannot discard the theme beside it. Nested objects combine, ordered lists and plain values replace, and an explicit null erases a key — the same rules the space theme patch follows. Add `?dryRun=true` to see the key-by-key diff without writing.

**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Use true or false (true/1/yes/on and false/0/no/off are accepted).

warnings.description: Values we ACCEPTED and then rewrote, one sentence each — a slugified tag, a normalised colour, a clamped range, a slug that was taken. **Absent when nothing was rewritten**, never `[]`. The same sentences are on the `X-Field-Warnings` response header. If this is present, something you sent is not what is stored; read the resource back rather than assuming your own value.

400.description: The request could not be understood — a malformed header, path or query value (`request.malformed`). A value that was understood but is not acceptable is a 422 `validation.failed`.

401.description: No credential, or one that is expired or revoked (`auth.required`). Send a Bearer token or the session cookie.

403.description: Authenticated, and not allowed — always `rbac.forbidden`, whether what is missing is the capability, the token scope, or a resource the token is pinned away from. The message names the capability and, for a scope refusal, the scopes that would grant it. A refusal because of the PLAN is a 402 with `quota.exceeded`, not this.

404.description: No such thing — one of the ids in the path does not resolve, or resolves to something this caller may not see (`*.not_found`).

422.description: The body was understood and a value is unacceptable (`validation.failed`). `error.details` names the field paths.

429.description: Rate limited — see the RateLimit-* headers.

default.description: Error — the stable { error: { code, message } } envelope.

Up to 2,000,000 characters of Markdown — the same ceiling the importer, the create and the update doors all use, so an imported page can always be written back.

**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.
delete.summary: Delete the front page in an organization

get.description:
The newest 100 preview links minted for this site, revoked and expired ones included (`active` says which still work). The token itself is never listed — it is shown once, when minted.

**Requires token scope: `read`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 100. 500 is the most this endpoint serves — a larger value is capped, not refused. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 422, never a silent default.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Where to continue from: pass back the `page.nextCursor` of the previous answer. Opaque — there is nothing inside one to construct or parse. Sending one also opts into the enveloped shape, exactly as stating `Forumulate-Version` does.

data.description: The same rows as the key named after them (`topics`, `articles`, `pages`, `monitors`, …), under a key that is the same on every paged list — so one parser reads every collection. The SAME array, not a different selection: read either. Present whenever `page` is, i.e. when you state `Forumulate-Version` (or send a `cursor`); the unversioned shape does not carry it.

200.description: The request's state. Our fulfilment is a database read, so a verified id is always `completed`. On an ACCESS request `resultUrl` is an absolute, public URL to the export bundle itself (bytes, not a pointer to fetch elsewhere) — present the same credential to it. A DELETION carries no `resultUrl`: it was performed when the request was opened and there is nothing to hand back. A request belongs to the organization it was opened for and answers 404 on any other one, so an id cannot be replayed to collect another tenant's view of the same person.

put.description:
Reads one document describing what this organization should have — spaces, their theme, redirects, collections, forum categories, status monitors, and org-level AI knowledge sources — and reports a per-unit DIFF against what is there today. **Nothing is written unless you send `?apply=true`.** Idempotent: applying the same manifest twice does the work once, and the second run answers `unchanged` for every unit. Additive: anything present that the manifest does not declare is reported under `extras` and never deleted. Each block is validated by the schema of the endpoint that owns it, so the manifest accepts exactly what those endpoints accept, and each unit re-checks that endpoint’s own capability — a dry run is refused wherever the apply would be. An apply is NOT one transaction (each subsystem opens its own, which is where tenant isolation lives); it is a sequence of idempotent units that stops at the first failure and names where it stopped, so a partial apply is resumed by fixing the manifest and applying again. The vocabulary for `type`, and which blocks a given type may declare, come from `GET /space-types`.

**Requires token scope: `write`** (the coarse method gate) for Atlas key (`ak_`), Personal Access Token (`cft_`) or OAuth (`cfo_`) auth — *in addition to* any catalog scope (`GET /pats/scopes`) the route’s capability needs. Session/cookie auth is governed by RBAC capabilities instead.

parameters.description: Use true or false (true/1/yes/on and false/0/no/off are accepted).

seed.description: Whether to create the starter structure this kind of space ships with. Left unset it follows who is asking: a console session gets it (an empty space is a worse first screen than an example one), a personal access token does not — an agent creating a space is about to write its own structure, and ours arrives as content it has to find and delete first.

preset.description: One of this space type's named layouts, as published by `GET /space-types`. Unset means the recommended one, resolved at read — so an improvement to the default reaches every space that never chose. An unknown name for the type is a 422 that lists the valid ones.

An icon name from `GET /icons?for=header` (see the `HeaderIconName` enum: our glyphs, the extended set and the brand marks), or an image URL (https://…, /api/assets/…, or a data: PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF — not SVG). Any other bare word is refused.

enabled.description: `false` hides the switcher (the same as `placement: "none"`). Unset: shown.

placement.description: Where the content-language switcher sits: header (the nav bar's end) | header-start | header-overflow (the header menu) | sidebar | footer | content-top | floating | none. Unset: the surface’s own place (docs: sidebar; others: content-top).

style.description: `select` (unset): the reader dropdown, from the control tokens. `pills`: a row of links. `compact`: a tight row of codes (EN · ES).

names.description: How each language is named: native (unset, "Español"), english ("Spanish"), code ("ES").

flags.description: A flag before each name. Off by default.

flagCountries.description: The country whose flag stands for a language: `{ "en": "US", "pt-BR": "BR" }`.

locales.description: Which languages are listed, in order (codes; `default` = the original). Unset: all declared.

customLabels.description: A label per language code (`default` = the original), over `names`.

missing.description: When this page has no translation in a language: home (unset — that language’s front door), disabled (listed, not a link), hide (only languages this page is translated into).

remember.description: Keep the reader’s pick, so a page in another language offers its translation. Never changes a page’s own language. Off by default.

from.description: The path to redirect FROM, relative to the space’s mount. A trailing `*` matches everything below it: `/old/*` matches `/old/a` and `/old/a/b`. The longest matching wildcard wins, and an exact rule always beats a wildcard.

to.description: Where to send it: a bare path (relative to this space’s mount) or an absolute `https://` URL, which means exactly what it says. A trailing `*` here carries the part the `from` wildcard matched — `/old/* → /new/*` sends `/old/a/b` to `/new/a/b`; without it, every match lands on the one address.

type.description: `redirect` (the default) sends the reader to `to`. `rewrite` serves `to` at the address that was asked for, without changing the URL. A rewrite names a path of this same space — an absolute `to` is refused, because a rewrite is not a proxy.

status.description: The redirect’s HTTP status: 301, 302, 307 or 308. Default 308 (permanent, keeps the method). Not allowed on a rewrite, which answers whatever `to` answers.

query.description: Query-string conditions. A map of key → exact value: every listed pair must be present for the rule to match (other keys are allowed). `"ignore"` — the default — matches whatever the query is. Among rules with the same `from`, the one with more conditions is tried first.

passQuery.description: `true` carries the incoming query string to the target (merged under any query the target already has); `false` drops it. Unset keeps it on a same-host redirect and drops it on an off-site one. A rewrite always keeps it.

redirects.description: The whole table, replacing what is stored — except the rules the platform wrote itself when a page or a collection was renamed, which are kept unless your list claims the same `from`. Renaming a collection moves one address — its hub, `/c/<slug>` — and we write that rule for you; the pages filed under it are addressed by their own slug within the space and do not move.

icon.description: An icon name from `GET /icons?for=page` (see the `PageIconName` enum), an emoji or short symbol (≤ 8 characters, no "/" or ":"), or an image URL. Any other bare word is refused: the reader would print it as text.

anyOf.description: An icon name from `GET /icons?for=header` (see the `HeaderIconName` enum: our glyphs, the extended set and the brand marks), or an image URL (https://…, /api/assets/…, or a data: PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF — not SVG). Any other bare word is refused.

icon.description: An icon name from `GET /icons?for=header` (see the `HeaderIconName` enum: our glyphs, the extended set and the brand marks), or an image URL (https://…, /api/assets/…, or a data: PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF — not SVG). Any other bare word is refused.

kind.description: `http` (default) polls `url`; `heartbeat` waits for your job to ping; `manual` is probed by nothing — its state is `declaredState` (else operational) or what an open incident linked to it says; `space` rolls up another status page of this organization (`targetSpaceId`) on a hub page; `statuspage` mirrors a vendor’s public Statuspage (`url`, plus `vendorComponent`). Fixed at creation: a PATCH cannot turn one kind into another — delete and re-create instead.

targetSpaceId.description: Kind `space`: the status page it rolls up (state, uptime and days are that page’s).

vendorComponent.description: Kind `statuspage`: the vendor component’s id or exact name in its summary.json. Null: the vendor page’s overall indicator.

region.description: Where it runs ("EU", "US-East"). `theme.status.components.groupBy: region` groups by it.

description.description: What the component is, in a sentence — shown to readers beside its name.

slug.description: Its stable address within the page (component page, per-component subscription), normalised to lowercase words joined by hyphens. Minted from the name on create when omitted; unique per page — a taken one is a 409. Renaming the component does not move it.

linkUrl.description: Where the component’s own docs or product live; its name links there.

display.description: `bars` (default) draws its day bars; `status` only its state; `hidden-unless-degraded` leaves it off the page while it is operational.

startsOn.description: The day it started existing. Earlier days draw as "not yet" rather than as no data. Null: from its first check (a `manual` component: from the day it was created).

intervalSeconds.description: Seconds between checks (`http`, clamped to 30–3600, default 60) or the longest wait for a ping (`heartbeat`, clamped to 60–604800, default 3600). PATCH clamps by the same rule.

audience.description: Who may see this on the public page: `everyone` (default), `signedIn` (any signed-in reader) or `groups` (a signed-in member of one of `groups`). Hidden rows are dropped by the API before anything is sent. The machine doors — `summary.json`, `api/v2`, the feeds, the badge and the widget — always answer as an anonymous reader.

declaredState.description: A state a person declares, which wins over the checks until it is cleared with `null`. Every field of this body — this one, `alertsEnabled` and both thresholds included — is applied on create exactly as on PATCH.
